messages:
maria: quick check — saw a repro where a prefetched prefix is still returned after a demote+evict, causing stale tokens to be used by the read path. seems like the handshake promise (claim->ack->commit) isn't always synchronized with demote visibility in the observer. anyone seen this?
aj: yup saw similar in canary yesterday. root cause looked like double-fastpath: local cache served while handoff in-flight.
ken: is this the case where demote sets residency=false but we still have an in-flight prefetch future that writes back a stale residency?
clara: that matches my trace. prefetch future completes after demote but we don't check epoch token on writeback. writeback rehydrates slab and makes the prefix appear live again.
maria: exact. two questions: 1) do we require writeback to verify lease/epoch before making prefix visible? 2) can we accept a short window where reads may get stale if it simplifies handshake?
aj: for 1) i'd expect a CAS against epoch/generation. we already carry lease_epoch in the prefetch response. cheap check: compare current_epoch() before commit.
ken: cheap check is fine but introduces a race where epoch increments between check and commit. need CAS on metadata. we have a small on-disk compare-and-swap path in the sidecar that could work.
clara: CAS path adds latency; this is on the hot path for some workloads. alternative: treat prefetch writeback as "best-effort" and publish a tombstone when demote happens that invalidates later writebacks. then writeback checks tombstone.
pavel: tombstone idea is reasonable. tombstones are already in the demote flow for compaction. we could piggyback a prefix-epoch counter as tombstone marker. writeback reads prefix_meta and aborts if tombstone_epoch > prefetch_epoch.
maria: that would avoid extra locks. tradeoff: tombstone propagation lag could still allow a brief stale window. is that acceptable for correctness?
aj: depends on SLA. for strong R/W we need linearizable semantics -> CAS. for soft correctness (we call it eventual-evict) tombstone approach is fine and simpler.
ken: ops question: how will this interact with multi-tenant sharing across slabs? tombstone propagation must be per-tenant and fast else we leak cross-tenant hotness.
clara: implement tombstone push to tenant observer; observer applies immediately in-memory and sets a short grace TTL for writebacks to consult. should be O(1) latency within node.
ops-bot: note: increased tombstone checks = +0.8% CPU in benchmark sim earlier today (see link). :eyes:
maria: another angle: what about prefetch cancellation on demote? if we can cancel inflight prefetches reliably that's ideal. but cancellation isn't always possible if network or rpc already completed.
pavel: true. cancel best-effort + tombstone CAS hybrid seems robust: try cancel, if cancel fails rely on tombstone CAS compare at commit.
aj: we should add metrics: prefetch-cancel-failures, writeback-aborts-due-to-tombstone, and stale-serve-detected. that will help tune grace window.
ken: one more boundary: public API for prefix "pin" vs "soft-pin". if user pins, we must prevent demote entirely. soft-pin allows demote but tries to rehydrate. we need clear semantics to avoid customer surprises.
clara: agree. pin -> strong lease + no tombstone allowed. soft-pin -> tombstone allowed but with longer tombstone propagation TTL and different demote heuristics.
maria: action items: 1) prototype tombstone epoch check in prefetch writeback (pavel + clara) 2) instrument metrics (aj) 3) small doc describing pin vs soft-pin semantics (ken) 4) follow up canary once prototype + metrics wired (maria)
aj: ok i'll add metrics PR by EOD.
clara: i'll spike tombstone prototype tomorrow and link results.
pavel: will help with observer propagation hook.
ken: i'll draft pin semantics doc in #docs later today.
maria: thanks all. if anyone has small repro clips post them here (esp traces showing writeback after demote). :thumbsup:
